text: Furthermore, when two neurons closely located to the same electrode fire an action potential at the same time, it will lead to an overlap of the waveforms in the recorded signal. This overlapping signal will not match any of the templates and will therefore often be missed by the sorter [ 17 ]. Finally, template matching based algorithms and other automated post-hoc clustering-based methods [ 18 , 19 ] require all spikes in the recording to be pooled together before performing the clustering. As a result, spike sorting can only be performed after a recording is finished, leaving it impossible to know to which neuron a detected spike belongs while an experiment is ongoing.
source_label: RT-Sort: An action potential propagation-based algorithm for real time spike detection and sorting with millisecond latencies
